report.summary: Reviewed base.py: defines ProviderCapabilities and Provider ABC with one concrete helper method.

handoff.purpose: Define base provider interface and capabilities dataclass.

symbols.name: ProviderCapabilities
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass with fields name, can_write, local, trusted_with_ip, agentic.

symbols.name: Provider
symbols.note: Abstract base class with abstract methods available() and run(), and concrete helper _enforce_read_only().

symbols.name: _enforce_read_only
symbols.note: Helper that mutates a report dict to enforce read-only policy.

claims.text: What a provider is *allowed* and *able* to do. These are structural guarantees enforced by the harness, not promises the model must keep.
claims.why: The docstring describes the class as defining capabilities, which matches the code (dataclass fields).

claims.text: may mutate the repo (apply edits / run tools)
claims.why: Field is boolean and named can_write, consistent with the comment.

claims.text: runs on this machine; no network egress at all
claims.why: Field is boolean and named local, consistent with the comment.
Field is boolean and named trusted_with_ip, consistent with the comment.

claims.text: can read the repo itself vs. needs inlined context
claims.why: Field is boolean and named agentic, consistent with the comment.

claims.text: Common interface for every model backend. All providers return the same validated ``agent_report_v1`` dict so everything downstream is uniform.
claims.why: The docstring mentions 'agent_report_v1' dict, but the chunk does not define or validate that structure. The return type of run() is dict[str, Any], which is consistent but not verified.

claims.text: True if this provider can be reached right now (key set / server up).
claims.why: Method signature returns bool, docstring describes a boolean condition.
The docstring specifies keys in the return dict, but the code only declares return type as dict[str, Any]. The actual keys are not enforced in this chunk.

claims.text: A read-only provider can neither edit files nor run tests. Any change it proposes is advisory: it is moved into ``handoff.suggestions`` and the mutating fields are forced empty so nothing can be auto-applied.
claims.why: The method checks self.caps.can_write; if false, it moves proposed files to handoff.suggested_files, clears files_changed and tests_run, and downgrades status from 'done' to 'needs_review'. This matches the claim.

observations.what: Method _enforce_read_only accesses self.caps.can_write, which relies on the subclass setting the caps attribute. The attribute is not initialized in the base class.
The docstring of _enforce_read_only mentions 'handoff.suggestions', but the code uses 'handoff.suggested_files'. This discrepancy could cause confusion.
The method modifies the report dict in-place and also returns it. Callers may rely on either behavior.
